title: Prescriptions Training Note: Counting the Lost Days on a Replaced Refill
content:
When a Kestrel Prescriptions refill is lost or stolen, the theft replacement lost days are the days of the replaced refill — the prescription's most recent refill — that the replacement makes good.

## The rule

The theft replacement lost days are worked out by the first case that fits, the pickup being the pickup entry that names the replaced refill:

1. **Picked up on a later day than it was dispensed:** its days supply dispensed less the calendar days from that pickup date, as day 0, to today, never below zero.
2. **Never picked up:** its whole days supply dispensed counts.
3. **Otherwise** (picked up on the day it was dispensed): its days supply dispensed less the calendar days from its dispensing date, as day 0, to today, never below zero.

## Worked through (hypothetical refill of 30 days dispensed on day 0, today is day 10)

| Pickup of the replaced refill | Case | Lost days |
|---|---|---|
| day 4 | 1 | 30 less 6: 24 |
| never picked up | 2 | 30 |
| day 0 | 3 | 30 less 10: 20 |
| day 2, with today day 45 | 1 | 30 less 43, never below zero: 0 |

**Why does a late pickup matter?** The count runs from the day the patient actually collected the refill when that was later than the dispensing date.
